categories.name: Rain notes
categories.description: Weather, the street and the shop on wet days.

categories.name: Making
categories.description: Frames, canopies and finishing at the bench.

posts.title: The first autumn shower
posts.excerpt: Shigure is the rain that comes and goes in an afternoon. This week it came three times before closing.
posts.content:
Shigure is the rain that comes and goes in an afternoon. This week it came three times before closing, and each time the street emptied and filled again.

Under the awning

People wait under the shop awning for the shower to pass. Some of them try a canopy while they wait; one left with the Kasa Sixteen over her shoulder and the sun already out.

We keep a basket of lending umbrellas by the door for days like this. Bring them back when it suits you.

posts.title: Splitting bamboo for a frame
posts.excerpt: Forty-eight ribs from one cane: why we split them in order and number each one.
posts.content:
A paper umbrella has forty-eight ribs, and every one of them comes from the same cane. We split them in order and pencil a number on each, so they close back into the same place.

Why one cane

Bamboo from one cane bends the same way. Ribs from different canes pull the canopy out of round within a season.

The cane dries for a year in the loft before we touch it.

posts.title: Drying an umbrella properly
posts.excerpt: Most repairs we see start the same way: an umbrella furled wet and left in a stand.
posts.content:
Most repairs we see start the same way: an umbrella furled wet and left in a stand. The tips rust, the stitching rots and the runner sticks.

Halfway open

Open it halfway in the hall or the bath, away from a heater, until the fabric is dry to the touch. Then furl it loosely.

Paper umbrellas should dry fully open, crown down, in the shade.

posts.title: A frame from 1962, mended
posts.excerpt: A customer brought in her grandfather’s umbrella. The frame was sound; everything else needed help.
posts.content:
A customer brought in her grandfather’s umbrella, bought on this street in 1962. The frame was sound; the canopy, the runner and two ribs were not.

What we kept

We kept the steel ribs, the crown and the handle, re-covered it in grey cotton and made a new runner to the old pattern.

It took three weeks. It will need us again in another sixty years.

posts.title: Packing in a cotton sleeve
posts.excerpt: Every umbrella leaves furled in a cotton sleeve with its care card, wrapped in plain paper.
posts.content:
Every umbrella leaves furled in a cotton sleeve with its care card, wrapped in plain paper and tied with a cotton tape.

No plastic

The sleeve is the same cotton as our canopies. It keeps the umbrella clean in a bag, and it is the sleeve we ask you to post it back in for repairs.

posts.title: Rain on the river street
posts.excerpt: On wet afternoons the shop is quietest and busiest at once.
posts.content:
On wet afternoons the shop is quietest and busiest at once: no one passes, and everyone who does comes in.

The sound of it

A good canopy makes one sound in the rain, a soft drumming. Rattles and flaps mean a loose tip or a slack gore, and we would like to hear about them.

products.name: Hoshikawa Long
products.short: A long umbrella of slate-blue oiled cotton on a bamboo shaft, finished with a cord-wrapped tip and a plain bamboo crook.
products.description:
A long umbrella of slate-blue oiled cotton on a bamboo shaft, finished with a cord-wrapped tip and a plain bamboo crook.

We split the bamboo for the shaft and runner from one cane, so the colour of the wood runs the whole length. The canopy is a tightly woven cotton, oiled twice and left to cure for a week before it is sewn on.

Canopy 104 cm across on 24 ribs · Slate-blue oiled cotton on a bamboo frame · 520 g.

Care: open it halfway to dry, never furl it wet. Repairs at the counter for as long as the frame is sound.

details.Canopy: Slate-blue oiled cotton on a bamboo frame

products.name: Ame Fold
products.short: A three-fold compact in pale grey, light enough for a coat pocket and strong enough for a windy bridge.
products.description:
A three-fold compact in pale grey, light enough for a coat pocket and strong enough for a windy bridge.

The frame folds in three on fibreglass-tipped steel ribs, with a soft-close runner so it never snaps shut on a finger. The canopy is a dense recycled polyester with a quiet matt finish.

Canopy 96 cm across on 8 ribs · Pale grey recycled polyester, three-fold steel frame · 310 g.

Care: open it halfway to dry, never furl it wet. Repairs at the counter for as long as the frame is sound.

details.Canopy: Pale grey recycled polyester, three-fold steel frame

products.name: Kasa Sixteen
products.short: Sixteen ribs and a mist-grey waxed canopy: our everyday long umbrella, round and calm in a downpour.
products.description:
Sixteen ribs and a mist-grey waxed canopy: our everyday long umbrella, round and calm in a downpour.

Sixteen ribs keep the canopy almost perfectly round, so rain runs off evenly and the edge never flaps. The crook handle is bent from one length of ash and stained near-black, then oiled, not lacquered.

Canopy 110 cm across on 16 ribs · Mist-grey waxed cotton, black crook handle · 480 g.

Care: open it halfway to dry, never furl it wet. Repairs at the counter for as long as the frame is sound.

details.Canopy: Mist-grey waxed cotton, black crook handle

products.name: Tsuyu Paper
products.short: A paper umbrella for the rainy season: deep slate oiled washi over thirty-six bamboo ribs, with a plain bamboo shaft.
products.description:
A paper umbrella for the rainy season: deep slate oiled washi over thirty-six bamboo ribs, with a plain bamboo shaft.

The washi is brushed with oil three times and dried in the shade between coats, which gives the deep slate its soft sheen. Threaded by hand at the crown so the canopy opens into a calm, even dome.

Canopy 104 cm across on 36 ribs · Deep slate oiled washi on thirty-six bamboo ribs · 560 g.

Care: open it halfway to dry, never furl it wet. Repairs at the counter for as long as the frame is sound.

details.Canopy: Deep slate oiled washi on thirty-six bamboo ribs

products.name: Kiri Mini
products.short: Our smallest folding umbrella: six ribs, a fog-grey canopy and a sleeve that fits a jacket pocket.
products.description:
Our smallest folding umbrella: six ribs, a fog-grey canopy and a sleeve that fits a jacket pocket.

An aluminium frame keeps it under a quarter of a kilo. It is the umbrella we hand to visitors who arrive without one.

Canopy 88 cm across on 6 ribs · Fog-grey polyester, aluminium frame · 240 g.

Care: open it halfway to dry, never furl it wet. Repairs at the counter for as long as the frame is sound.

products.name: Bangasa Twilight
products.short: A traditional paper umbrella: forty-eight split bamboo ribs under oiled washi, threaded by hand at the crown.
products.description:
A traditional paper umbrella: forty-eight split bamboo ribs under oiled washi, threaded by hand at the crown.

Each rib is split, shaved and numbered so it closes back into the same place. The washi is oiled with persimmon tannin and linseed and dried in the shade, which keeps it waterproof for years if it is opened to dry after use.

Canopy 112 cm across on 48 ribs · Persimmon-oiled washi paper on forty-eight bamboo ribs · 690 g.

Care: open it halfway to dry, never furl it wet. Repairs at the counter for as long as the frame is sound.

details.Canopy: Persimmon-oiled washi paper on forty-eight bamboo ribs

products.name: Ferrule Cane
products.short: A walking-length umbrella with a chestnut shaft and a turned brass ferrule that taps quietly on stone.
products.description:
A walking-length umbrella with a chestnut shaft and a turned brass ferrule that taps quietly on stone.

The shaft is a single length of chestnut, long enough to lean on. The ferrule is turned from brass and fitted with a replaceable rubber cap.

Canopy 100 cm across on 8 ribs · Storm-grey oiled cotton, chestnut shaft, brass ferrule · 560 g.

Care: open it halfway to dry, never furl it wet. Repairs at the counter for as long as the frame is sound.

details.Canopy: Storm-grey oiled cotton, chestnut shaft, brass ferrule

products.name: Hoshi Child
products.short: A small long umbrella for children: rounded rib tips, a soft-close runner and a short, light shaft.
products.description:
A small long umbrella for children: rounded rib tips, a soft-close runner and a short, light shaft.

Rounded caps on every rib tip and a runner that will not pinch. The canopy is low enough to see through the clear window panel sewn into one gore.

Canopy 78 cm across on 8 ribs · Pale blue cotton, rounded tips, short shaft · 280 g.

Care: open it halfway to dry, never furl it wet. Repairs at the counter for as long as the frame is sound.
